Introducing the 2027 Block of the Month: Feels Like Home

by Suzy Williams

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 10:26
Instaread

I can’t hold it in any longer! This is our 2027 Block of the Month sampler quilt! Eeeeek! The theme of the year is “Feels Like Home.”

This design is a modern take on the classic medallion quilt, inspired by traditional folk motifs and the idea that home is what you make it.

Just as the places that feel most like home are built over time piece by piece, each month, we’ll add another layer to the medallion and watch the quilt grow, section by section and season by season. In December, we’ll have a finished quilt—and a reminder that when we make space for one another, we create something beautiful together.

You can sign up NOW through The Cutting Table! We will have lots of kits available for presale over the next couple of months. These will all ship in early December or before, so you are ready to start sewing in January.

2027 Block of the Month Kits

We will add more kits over the next couple of months, including some with the new Picnic Wovens 2 collection! Sign up for our newsletter to be up to date with what we offer.

Did You Know?

Did you know that our past three Block of the Month quilts all use 16" square blocks? This was intentional for two reasons.

  1. As we worked through new blocks each month, I wanted you to have the opportunity to substitute blocks from past BOMs into the current design. Just in case you really didn't want to make one of the blocks, you wouldn't need to give up entirely.
  2. We have a lot of very cool bonus tutorials using BOM blocks. Did you know that most of those bonus tutorials could be made with other 16" blocks from different months? Take the pie carrier pattern, for example. You could substitute the apple block from the 2026 March BOM instead of the original star block from the 2024 BOM. So fun!

What is a Medallion Quilt?

Since this is our fourth Block of the Month quilt, I thought it was time to shake things up a bit! Instead of making 12 square blocks, we're going to build a medallion quilt. I know those 16" squares were a lot of fun, but I think you're going to love this new approach, too.

So, what exactly is a medallion quilt? It's a quilt built around a central design, with multiple borders radiating outward to frame it. Those borders can be pieced, appliquéd, embroidered, or any combination of the three. Think of it as building a quilt from the inside out, with each new border adding another layer of color, pattern, and personality.

Medallion quilts have a long history! The style was popular in Europe before becoming a favorite among American quiltmakers in the late 1700s and early 1800s. In fact, you'll sometimes see them called framed quilts in British quilting history. Early makers often featured stars, floral bouquets, or elaborate appliqué in the center, then surrounded those designs with carefully arranged borders. Some quilts were strikingly symmetrical, while others took a more playful, asymmetrical approach, like our 2027 BOM.

By the 1840s, block-style quilts featuring repeating patterns had become increasingly popular, and the medallion style became less dominant. But it never disappeared! Today, medallion quilts are enjoying renewed interest among modern quilters, proving that a great design idea never really goes out of style.

I love that a medallion gives us a different way to think about quiltmaking. Rather than piecing individual blocks and arranging them into rows, we'll watch our quilt grow outward, one border at a time.

2027 BOM Fabric Requirements

As with all Suzy Quilts patterns published in the last two years, we include fabric requirements for both 42" and 57" wide fabric. Most quilting cotton is 42" wide, and all of my woven collections are 57" wide.

Most Popular Tutorials From The Cutting Table

We're about to wrap up our fourth year of The Cutting Table, and we've packed a lot of creativity into those four years! Annual subscribers now have access to more than 200 tutorials and articles, all filled with beautiful, fun-to-make sewing projects. We love challenging ourselves to come up with new ideas, and we're so happy to have you along for the ride.

Keep reading to discover some of the most popular tutorials from The Cutting Table. And if you haven't joined us yet, come be part of the fun! Along with our growing library of tutorials, you'll get access to our Block of the Month and a coupon code for a free pattern from our shop every month. That's a $180 value in patterns alone!

Honestly, what are you waiting for?

Pie Carrier Pattern

Here at The Cutting Table, we've seen many projects go viral. One of our most popular tutorials ever is this sweet and simple pie carrier. Originally designed as a bonus project in our 2024 Block of the Month, the pie carrier took on a life of its own when we first posted it on Instagram. You all really love pie!

Upcycled Crossbody Bag Tutorial

Fanny packs are making a comeback, and honestly, we’re stumped as to why something so convenient ever went out of style. In this tutorial, we’ll show you how to upcycle denim into a versatile bag that can be worn as either a crossbody bag or fanny pack. The strap is also detachable, so you can make multiple straps to interchange with your denim bag — fashion and versatility, baby!

Ironing Board Cover Tutorial

Is your ironing board cover in a sad state? Maybe the cover is scorched and stained, and the fabric itself doesn't match your taste or look cute in your sewing room — it is definitely time for a refresh! A new cover is relatively easy to buy, and there are cute designer ones out there. BUT! What if you made your own, out of materials you already have on hand, and it was the perfect vibe to jumpstart your sewjo this season? YES, PLEASE! A custom ironing board cover is easy to make, and this one is fitted to the exact size of the board you have. You could even use seasonal fabric to coordinate with the holidays!

Reversible Ric-Rac Napkins Tutorial

Make a set of sweet ric-rac napkins perfect for afternoon tea. The napkin set in this tutorial is a lovely combination of soft chambrays and silky Tana lawns adorned with coordinating ric-rac trim. The extra ric-rac touch gives them an elegant, vintage feel. These are perfect for tea with friends or to add to a child's special tea party.

Strawberry Coin Purse Pattern

The most popular project ever in The Cutting Table! Add a pop of charm to your everyday carry with this adorable strawberry-shaped coin purse! Perfect for coins, earbuds, or small essentials — even a mini sewing kit — it’s a fun and functional sewing project that makes a sweet gift or cute addition to your bag. Plus, who doesn’t love sewing something this *berry* cute?! 

Casserole Carrier Tutorial

Whether you’re heading to a potluck or just bringing dinner to a friend, keeping your casserole warm and stylishly transported is essential. This quilted casserole carrier — made using the ninth block in The Cutting Table’s 2025 botanically themed block of the month (BOM) — is a practical and beautiful solution that blends function with a touch of handmade love.

Roll-Up Picnic Placemats Tutorials

These roll-up picnic placemats were one of our 2024 bonus projects from The Cutting Table's Block of the Month. Perfect for warm weather, these placemats are easy to transport to your favorite picnic spot. Having lunch on the porch? Your napkin and silverware will stay securely in place with the built-in pocket. No worrying about the wind with these placemats! And not only are they stylish, but they're also practical and eco-friendly.

Signature Quilt Block Tutorial

In this scrap-friendly tutorial, you’ll learn how to create a signature block that can be used to make a pillow, quilt, or other project. The signature block features a light-colored center square where you (or others!) can sign and/or write directly onto the fabric.  

In this tutorial, we’ll walk you through the steps of creating an 8" signature block, share our recommended fabric-writing tools, and inspire you with a few ideas for projects that use a signature block, like the family "yearbook" quilt we put together. 

Sunglasses Case Tutorial

This snap-top sunglasses case is fun, fast, and inexpensive to sew, and it’ll keep your shades looking good all summer long. You can buy special hardware to make a snap-top pouch, but in this tutorial, we share a little secret to make your own using affordable tools you probably have on hand.

The size of the case is customizable. A smaller size pouch is perfect for turning a gift card into a special gift. Or try sewing a larger pouch to hold your charging cords when traveling or a little sewing kit, a tablet, or even dog treats!

Tulip Bag Pattern

This tulip bag is a unique shape that will become a spring staple of your wardrobe. Inspired by the curves of tulip petals, this is one project where you don't need to feel intimidated to sew curves. These gentle curves are beginner-friendly and the bag comes together quickly! 

Ruffle Tote Bag Pattern

Back by popular demand! We know how much you loved our ruffle pillow tutorial, so we knew it was time to add ruffles to another favorite — this time, a tote bag. Both practical and pretty, ruffles add a soft, feminine touch to an everyday bag. In this ruffle tote bag tutorial, we walk you through sewing a tote that’s both functional and full of charm.

Basket Block Quilt Tutorial

Inspired by the baskets that hold sewing notions, this basket block tutorial can be used to make pillows, quilts, or whatever your quilty heart desires! This traditional quilt design uses color blocking in a way that makes it feel modern. If you choose to use solid fabrics, it will feel even more modern.

Pieced versions of the basket block have appeared in quilts since at least the mid-1800s (with quilted and appliquéd versions dating even earlier), and the block has remained a popular quilting motif that's steeped in the utility of an item commonly used by people — especially women — for hundreds of years. This tutorial walks you through the steps to make a basket block and your own basket quilt in one of two sizes: baby (48 1/2" square) or throw (70" square). 

We also have a video tutorial on sewing this decorative binding stitch seen below!

Felt Bird Ornament Pattern

This felt bird ornament pattern is great for hte holiday season. You won't spend weeks laboring over them — you can make a set in a day or two. During the busiest time of the year, the pull between making handmade gifts and spending quality time with the people you love is real for serious crafters. And sometimes, less is more with our handmade gifts. 

Quick gifts open up more time for all the special holiday events and parties you want to attend. And that time is a gift you can start giving yourself each year. Plus, these ornaments are beautiful and sophisticated. They'll wow anyone on your gift list!
